contract.application_algorithm_qualification: Application composition is fixture-authored; direct public API/native behavior supplies the SUT boundary.
cleanup: All actor handlers/transactions and gate timers must settle before audit/cleanup.
Every native SQL cursor is immediately drained, retained only for bounded final drain.
DeleteAll only on the correlated fresh owned root; verify KV empty and SQL application tables absent.
External supervisor must enforce independent deadlines/RSS and reap owned processes/store; receipts cannot self-prove placement or teardown.
contract.distinctness: D218 tests ingest parser boundaries and trigger row-count metadata. Here ordinary exec triggers maintain old/new relational aggregates across queued requests; sql.ingest is not used.
contract.failure_hypothesis: The update trigger may leave one folder charged, or later deletion could use stale pre-move totals.
contract.intent: Native INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger bodies maintain both sides of a collection move while explicit KV indexes follow the same transaction.
contract.left_checkpoint: Left moves a to y and resizes to5, holds before KV rekey.
contract.oracle: folders x count0/bytes0, y count1/bytes5; SQL only a/y/5; KV only y/a=5.
contract.os_evidence_status: RETAINED_PROVENANCE_ONLY: synthetic platform composition; no OS checkout/callsite was reread, and this is not an actual OS integration test.
preconditions: Exact pinned direct celld source and reviewed matching executable; no substitute runtime.
Fresh owned SQLite DO root, one stable activation, no preexisting KV or user SQL.
Two ordinary same-deployment DO.fetch requests must pre-enter one recipient before its transaction input gate closes.
All storage and SQL operations execute on real ctx.storage with public APIs and native SQLite.

source_refs.purpose: Real root transactions serialize distinct pre-entered request owners; ordinary input gate and transaction tail.
Public storage transaction controls map to native BEGIN IMMEDIATE, COMMIT and nested SAVEPOINT/RELEASE.
Public native SQL cursor shaping, typed bindings and finite draining.
Queries execute through native SQLite prepare/bind/step, not a JavaScript SQL emulator.
Ordinary application trigger definitions are allowed by authorizer.
